title: Article 257A — Assistance to States by deployment of armed forces (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 257A empowered the Union to deploy armed forces or other Union-controlled forces in a State to deal with grave law-and-order situations. It was inserted by the 42nd Amendment (Emergency-era centralisation) and omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, with effect from 20 June 1979, to restore federal balance. Deployment questions are now addressed under the general framework of Articles 355 and 356 and ordinary statutory powers.
content.glance: Art 257A omitted by 44th Amendment 1978 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). Inserted by 42nd Amendment; removed to restore Centre–State balance.
content.study:
Article 257A was a temporary centralising provision from the 42nd Amendment period. It authorised Union deployment of forces in States for serious internal situations beyond the ordinary assistance model.

Omission: Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979), as part of the post-Emergency rollback of several 42nd Amendment measures that were seen as undermining federalism.

Living frame: Union duties and emergency/internal-security powers are governed by Articles 355, 356 and applicable statutes; there is no separate Article 257A power.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 257A as living authority for force deployment.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Inserted during the Emergency-era 42nd Amendment package; omitted by the 44th Amendment, 1978 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). The omission was justified as restoring equilibrium between Centre and States on internal security deployment.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Link insertion to 42nd Amendment and omission to 44th Amendment.
2. Do not rely on Article 257A for current deployment analysis.
3. Use Articles 355/356 and statutory frameworks for modern questions.

examples.title: Illustration — Post-1979 deployment challenge
examples.body: A 2026 challenge that treats Article 257A as the source of Union deployment power is misconceived. The article stands omitted; analysis must proceed under living constitutional and statutory provisions.

misconceptions.trap: Article 257A still authorises Union force deployment in States.
misconceptions.correction: Article 257A was omitted by the 44th Amendment, 1978. It is not living law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 257A?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 257A was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). It is not living law. Current Centre–State force deployment issues fall under Articles 355, 356 and applicable statutes.

examTips: Pair 42nd (insert) with 44th (omit) when discussing Emergency-era centralisation rollbacks.
content.migrationNote: Remediated 2026-10-09: accurate 42nd insert / 44th omit history. Case-law gate open.

notes: Omission by 44th Amendment w.e.f. 20-6-1979 recorded from standard sources. No case holdings invented.

keyTakeaways: Inserted by 42nd Amendment; removed to restore federal balance.
